title: Redline priority heuristics & quick snips
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal scratchpad for triaging contract clauses during reviews and customer negotiations. Not a playbook — this is my fast checklist + refillable set of negotiation lines and redline snippets I actually copy/paste into review comments.

High-level heuristic (the 5-minute triage):
- Ask: does this clause affect run-of-business or catastrophic exposure?
  - Catastrophic = insolvency triggers, broad indemnities, unlimited liability, IP assignment, or customer audit that touches our infra.
  - Run-of-business = billing cadence, reporting, minor warranty wording, notice periods.
- Score: 1 (no-risk) — 5 (must-fix before signature).
  - 5 = block, escalate to GC + SRE + product; no go without sign-off.
  - 3 = standard redline language we can offer; usually acceptable with minor pushback.
  - 1–2 = accept or log as post-signature item.

Priority buckets (fast map):
- Tier A (immediate stop): unlimited/liability carveouts for customer damages, full IP assignment to customer, on-prem audit with admin access, data exfiltration indemnity that names our third-parties.
- Tier B (high): broad indemnities for any third-party claims (esp. data misuse), termination for convenience with no cure, SLA credits that cap at zero but create operational burden, mandatory security certifications we cant prove.
- Tier C (medium): payment timing (net-75), auto-renew notice shorter than 30 days, subcontractor lists, narrow force majeure?
- Tier D (low): formatting, notice addresses, non-material reporting frequencies.

Quick thresholds I use (copy into review comments):
- Liability cap: propose cap = greater of (fees paid in prior 12 months) x 3, or $250k for standard customers; escalate for enterprise deals.
- Exclusions from cap: personal injury, IP infringement where we indemnify, gross negligence / willful misconduct only.
- Indemnity: mutual-ish — customer indemnifies for data they upload that infringes IP; we indemnify for model IP infringement only if it arises from our codebase or willful misrelease.
- SLA credits: limited to service credits and not a deduction from fees; do not serve as sole remedy for security incidents.
- Termination for convenience: allow on customer side with 60 days notice; on our side only for material breach + cure or regulatory reasons.

Standard redline snippets (fast copy/paste):
- Liability cap snippet:
  "Notwithstanding anything to the contrary, Customer's and Provider's aggregate liability to each other shall not exceed the greater of (i) the total fees paid by Customer to Provider under the Statement of Work in the twelve (12) months preceding the event giving rise to liability, or (ii) Two Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars (USD $250,000). The foregoing cap shall not apply to liability arising from (a) a party's gross negligence or willful misconduct, (b) bodily injury or death, or (c) a party's breach of its confidentiality obligations involving personal data."

- Mutual IP indemnity starter:
  "Each party shall indemnify and hold harmless the other against all claims arising out of a third party allegation that the indemnifying party's pre-existing intellectual property, as provided to the other party under this Agreement, infringes a third party's intellectual property rights. The indemnifying party shall have sole control of the defense and settlement thereof, provided that the indemnified party may participate at its own expense."

- Data use / model outputs (sensitive):
  "Provider will use Customer Data solely to perform the Services and will not use Customer Data to further train models except as expressly agreed in writing. Aggregated, de-identified usage metrics may be used by Provider for product improvements provided such metrics cannot be re-identified to Customer or individual users."

Negotiation scripts (short lines for AMs/AE to use in threads):
- On liability cap asks: "Our standard cap is aligned to subscription volume — we can increase for enterprise deals if we have predictable revenue coverage. What contract value should we use to get you comfortable?"
- On audits: "We can provide SOC2 reports and redacted penetration test summaries. For operational audits that require access to production systems, we need a scoped, mutually agreed plan and a data processing addendum in place first."
- On IP assignment asks: "We cannot assign our underlying model or platform IP. We can grant a broad license to Customer for outputs and deliverables necessary to operate their product."

SRE-specific flags (ping SRE early):
- Any clause that requests "access to systems/logs with admin credentials" or live-streaming of requests.
- Retention requirement < 90 days for certain telemetry that we rely on for debugging (ask product whether feasible).
- Performance SLA that uses "99.99% availability of API" without defining maintenance windows or acceptable maintenance schedule — escalate.

Privacy/security quick checklist (fast pass):
- Data classification: is Customer data PII/regulated? If yes, add DPA and escalate to security.
- DPA templates: insist on our standard DPA; if customer redlines, capture specific asks and quantify risk (e.g., local cross-border restrictions).
- Subprocessors: require notice + objection process, not unlimited lists.

Escalation matrix (my shorthand):
- Tier A issues -> CC GC (Priya) + SRE lead (Mark) + AE + me. Pause counter-signature until resolved.
- Tier B -> CC me + Priya; try to negotiate mitigations (insurance, carveouts) within two rounds.
- Tier C/D -> we can handle offline in comments and accept with caveats.

Notes to self / TODOs during review:
- Inline comment for clause X: ask for specific examples of "Proprietary Data". If vague, propose a definition.
- If customer requests "delete on termination" for backups, confirm RTO/RPO impacts with infra team.
- Confirm whether customer needs export-control classification language for model weights. If yes, spin up legal convo.
- If deal > $1M ARR and customer pushes for unlimited liability, escalate immediately.

Post-signature remediation ideas (for product ops):
- Maintain a contract exceptions register with TTLs and owners. We should track any accepted deviations from standard terms and run quarterly reviews.
- For recurring credit disputes, propose a runbook for applying credits automatically and logging incident-level items to the console for audit.

Examples from recent deals (memory, for patterns):
- Large fintech asked for full source access for debugging -> denied; we offered redacted logs + joint debug sessions with scoped data.
- Education customer wanted outputs to be "works-for-hire" -> converted to a perpetual license for outputs only.
- EU telco wanted retention limited to 30 days -> negotiated 45 days for telemetry + possibility for extension upon justification.

Other quick heuristics:
- If a clause imposes obligations on "Provider and its affiliates" and includes downstream affiliates we don't control, confirm scope.
- Watch for one-sided audit or inspection rights that include non-customer data.
- Anything that tries to convert a licensing relationship into an employment-like obligation (e.g., specific staffing or subcontractor hiring requirements) -> flag.

Last-minute checklist before I send to GC: 
- Add citation to our contract playbook page (Confluence link) and any previous redlines for same customer.
- Summarize top 3 negotiation asks at the top of the redline comment thread.
- Confirm who on Sales will handle commercial concessions (discount, extended terms) if legal asks for trade-offs.

Random personal notes (brain dump):
- Want a one-pager cheat sheet for AEs listing "what we can concede vs must-defend" for common asks (liability, IP, audit, DPA). Build Q2 task?
- Consider templating a short negotiation email for low-value renewals asking for 60 days notice and auto-renew alignment.

-- end scratchpad --

(If this is still sitting here in 30 days, clean up and move snippets into the contract-library page.)
